items.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: For dances I had a band around town called the Futuristic Five... Walter Benton... played tenor, and I played alto and sang and got the gigs.

ctx.x: How did he feel about you — aspirations as a career in music?

He wasn’t too happy about it. Because I really didn’t start off to have a career in music. You just were going to play something. You’re going to do music. And then by the time I got out of high school I wanted to teach music. And my first two years in college that’s what I started out to be, a music teacher, and then I switched. But all during this time I © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

was performing. For dances I had a band around town called the Futuristic Five, and I was just talking to my friend the other night, I think I was one of the first women around L.A. during that time, early ‘50s and late ‘40s that had a band, had nerve enough to get a band.
